faq.a: Blocked conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate forces pyruvate to be reduced to lactate, raising serum lactate.
faq.q: Why does pyruvate carboxylase deficiency cause high lactate?

faq.a: Biotin is required for PC activity, but most PC mutations affect the protein core; supplementation rarely corrects severe deficiency.
PC deficiency shows isolated pyruvate‑to‑oxaloacetate block with normal respiratory chain enzymes; mtDNA disorders often have multi‑systemic signs and abnormal lactate/pyruvate ratios.
faq.q: How is the condition distinguished from mitochondrial DNA disorders?

exam: A 6‑month‑old presents with vomiting, lethargy, and a lactate of 8 mmol/L after a febrile illness – what is your next diagnostic step? — Check blood ammonia and consider PC deficiency if hyperammonemia accompanies lactic acidosis.
Explain why fasting precipitates a crisis in pyruvate carboxylase deficiency. — Fasting reduces acetyl‑CoA activation of PC, limiting oxaloacetate production and forcing pyruvate to lactate.

How would you differentiate PC deficiency from sepsis‑induced lactic acidosis in a rural clinic? — Look for chronic feeding intolerance, developmental delay, and hyperammonemia; sepsis usually has focal infection signs.

What bedside management should be started while awaiting confirmatory tests? — Initiate glucose infusion to suppress catabolism, correct acidosis with bicarbonate if pH <7.1, and avoid prolonged fasting.
Why is biotin not a reliable treatment for most PC deficiency cases? — Most pathogenic mutations affect the enzyme’s catalytic domain, not the biotin‑binding site.

List two tropical infections that can mimic the metabolic picture of PC deficiency and how to rule them out. — Malaria (check thick smear) and severe bacterial sepsis (full blood count, cultures); both have fever and lactate but lack hyperammonemia.
A child on a high‑carbohydrate diet develops worsening acidosis – what does this indicate about PC function? — Excess pyruvate overwhelms a deficient PC, increasing lactate production.
What long‑term monitoring is required for survivors of PC deficiency? — Regular growth charts, neurodevelopmental assessments, and periodic metabolic panels (lactate, ammonia).
ai.title: Pyruvate Carboxylase Deficiency
ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Pyruvate carboxylase (PC) is a mitochondrial enzyme that converts pyruvate to oxaloacetate, linking glycolysis to gluconeogenesis and the TCA cycle. Deficiency presents with lactic acidosis, neurologic regression, and failure to thrive, especially in low‑resource settings where early diagnosis is challenging.

b: Encoded by the PC gene on chromosome 11q13
Three isoforms: liver, brain, and kidney
sections.p: PC catalyses the ATP‑dependent carboxylation of pyruvate to oxaloacetate in mitochondria. It is essential for gluconeogenesis, anaplerosis of the TCA cycle, and fatty‑acid synthesis.

b: Provides substrate for glucose production during fasting
Supports neurotransmitter synthesis via TCA cycle intermediates
sections.p: Pyruvate + CO₂ + ATP → Oxaloacetate + ADP + Pi. Oxaloacetate can enter gluconeogenesis, replenish TCA intermediates, or be converted to malate for the malate‑aspartate shuttle.

b: Acetyl‑CoA acts as an allosteric activator
cAMP‑PKA phosphorylation enhances transcription in fasting
sections.p: PC activity is up‑regulated by acetyl‑CoA (signalling high‑energy status) and by glucagon‑cAMP pathways in liver. Biotin availability and mitochondrial health are also critical.

b: Severe form: early infantile onset, profound lactic acidosis, encephalopathy
Milder form: later onset, episodic hypoglycemia, developmental delay
sections.p: Autosomal recessive mutations in PC reduce enzyme activity, leading to impaired gluconeogenesis and anaplerosis. Accumulated pyruvate is shunted to lactate, causing metabolic acidosis.

b: Key triad: lactic acidosis, hyperammonemia, neurologic regression
sections.p: Patients present with poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, and rapid breathing. In low‑resource hospitals, the picture may be confused with sepsis, malaria, or HIV‑related metabolic crises.

t.b: Is there an anion‑gap metabolic acidosis? – Elevated >5 mmol/L supports PC deficiency
Is hyperammonemia present? – >100 µmol/L suggests impaired urea cycle secondary to TCA depletion
Detects elevated pyruvate and lactate metabolites – confirms a pyruvate metabolism disorder
Confirms diagnosis – not always available; use clinical criteria if unavailable

b: Remember biotin‑responsive forms of other carboxylases (e.g., pyruvate carboxylase vs. propionic acidemia)
In low‑resource settings, prioritize bedside clues: fasting intolerance, episodic encephalopathy
sections.p: Focus on the metabolic cascade, why lactic acidosis occurs, and how to differentiate PC deficiency from other causes of high lactate in a child.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe metabolic acidosis (pH <7.1) with rapid deterioration
Unexplained coma or seizures in an infant
